CheckTitle: Ensure IAM users receive permissions only through groups
Description: IAM policies must not be attached directly to individual users. Permissions should be granted via groups (for multiple users) or roles (for programmatic/federated access). Direct user policy attachment makes access management, auditing, and revocation significantly more complex.
Risk: Direct user policy attachments scatter access control across individual principals, making it difficult to audit who has what permissions, ensure consistent policy application, and quickly revoke access during an incident.
Remediation: Move all user-attached managed and inline policies to IAM groups or roles. Assign users to appropriate groups. Use IAM roles for service-to-service and federated access.
SeverityBasis: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0 Control 1.15 (Level 1); AWS Security Hub FSBP IAM.1 (ASFF score 64 / MEDIUM)
AuthoritativeSource: CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0; AWS Security Hub FSBP
